body: A&F Williams Street LLC, which bought the five-story office building at 165 Main Street in White Plains in 2014, sued the New York Power Authority on September 15, 2026 in Westchester County Supreme Court, alleging negligence and trespass, according to Westfair Communications. The building sits across from the former Galleria mall and next to NYPA's headquarters at 123 Main Street, separated from it by William Street, a short lane.

According to the complaint as reported by Westfair, A&F agreed last year to give NYPA access to its property for seven months to conduct a survey and install monitoring devices for a demolition and construction project at NYPA's parking garage, and NYPA agreed to fix any damage the project caused. A&F alleges the work produced excessive vibration that cracked its rooftop parapet and pulled a roofing membrane away from the masonry beneath it. It says it put up scaffolding to protect the public at a cost of $12,000 a month and that rebuilding the roof will cost more than $3 million. NYPA allegedly denied responsibility.

The complaint further alleges that on August 5, months after the access agreement expired, NYPA resumed construction within 30 feet of the building, and that tenants have complained about noise and dust, with some seeking rent reductions or lease terminations. It says NYPA "should have known" that demolition right next to an occupied commercial building risked structural damage. A&F seeks more than $3 million, an order holding NYPA responsible for repairs, and an order stopping demolition and construction until NYPA agrees to a reasonable access arrangement.
Asked for comment, a NYPA spokeswoman told Westfair that the authority does not comment on pending litigation. The allegations have not been tested in court.

timeline.label: A&F Williams Street LLC acquires the five-story office building at 165 Main Street, White Plains
A&F grants NYPA seven months of access to survey and install monitoring devices for the garage project
NYPA resumes construction within 30 feet of the building after the access agreement expired, the complaint alleges
A&F sues NYPA in Westchester County Supreme Court for negligence and trespass, seeking more than $3 million
